from itertools import combinations
from typing import List, Tuple


def pairwise_jaccard(method_circuits: Dict[str, Set[str]]) -> List[Tuple[str, str, float, int, int]]:
    results = []
    methods = sorted(method_circuits.keys())
    for m1, m2 in combinations(methods, 2):
        a, b = method_circuits[m1], method_circuits[m2]
        union = a | b
        inter = a & b
        jac = len(inter) / len(union) if union else 0.0
        results.append((m1, m2, jac, len(inter), len(union)))
    return results


def three_way_jaccard(method_circuits: Dict[str, Set[str]]) -> Tuple[float, int, int]:
    sets = list(method_circuits.values())
    inter = sets[0]
    union = sets[0]
    for s in sets[1:]:
        inter = inter & s
        union = union | s
    jac = len(inter) / len(union) if union else 0.0
    return jac, len(inter), len(union)


def print_pairwise_jaccard(pw: List[Tuple[str, str, float, int, int]], tw: Tuple[float, int, int]) -> None:
    print(f"\n{'='*50}")
    print("Pairwise Jaccard Decomposition")
    print(f"{'='*50}")
    for m1, m2, jac, inter, union in pw:
        print(f"  {m1} x {m2}: J={jac:.4f}  |A∩B|={inter}  |A∪B|={union}")
    jac3, inter3, union3 = tw
    print(f"  3-way:          J={jac3:.4f}  |A∩B∩C|={inter3}  |A∪B∪C|={union3}")
    print(f"{'='*50}\n")
